items.text: A federal rule barring Medicaid and CHIP money for puberty blockers, hormones and gender surgery for minors takes effect today in every state.
items.detail: The CMS final rule, published Aug. 13 (91 FR 52406), bars federal Medicaid funding for these procedures for patients under 18 and federal CHIP funding for those under 19. Children already on hormone therapy get up to six months of federal funding to taper; that transition does not cover puberty blockers or surgery. In New Hampshire, families suing in Goe v. HHS were denied a temporary restraining order on Oct. 5; their preliminary-injunction request is still pending, and no court has blocked the rule.
items.why: It ends federal payment for this care for low-income children nationwide, shifting the cost to states or families.

items.text: New drones and other devices built with chips or circuit boards from FCC blacklisted firms such as DJI can no longer win FCC approval, starting today.
items.detail: The FCC's Third Report and Order (FCC 26-50, ET Docket 21-232), published in the Federal Register Sept. 11, closes the "component part loophole" by barring authorization of devices that contain logic-bearing hardware made by Covered List entities, even if assembled in the U.S. It applies to applications filed on or after Oct. 13; already authorized equipment is unaffected, and pending applications are exempt unless amended to change such parts. It also requires online marketplaces to show the FCC ID at the point of sale.
items.why: It shuts a workaround U.S. assemblers used to keep selling new products built around Chinese drone and router parts.

items.text: A second drone attack in a week off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast sank one ship and damaged a Ukrainian-owned vessel, Bulgaria's prime minister said.
items.detail: Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the Maltese-flagged, Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3 was hit by three drones about 18 nautical miles off Bulgaria at about 1:30 a.m. Tuesday local time (6:30 p.m. ET Monday); its 15 crew were rescued and five got medical help. One crew member from the ship that sank was also rescued. Radev said there was no clear evidence who attacked but that "the outcome benefits" Russia, said Russia's ambassador would be summoned, and planned to speak with NATO chief Mark Rutte. Last week drones hit two ships off Bulgaria, sinking one whose 10 crew are still missing.
items.why: Repeated drone strikes next to a NATO member's waters raise the risk of the war spilling into the alliance.

items.text: The EU sanctioned nearly 1,600 Russian companies and executives in its largest listings package aimed at Moscow's military industry.
items.detail: The Council adopted 1,569 listings — 826 companies and 743 CEOs — targeting mid-level suppliers of electronics, missiles, drones and aircraft parts; more than half address ballistic-missile production. Listed people face asset freezes and EU travel bans, and the Ukraine territorial-integrity sanctions list now totals nearly 4,600. Separately the same day, the Council listed 77 people over illegal Russian State Duma elections in occupied Ukrainian territory.
items.why: The biggest EU listing round since 2022 raises pressure on Russia's war industry as Washington eases energy sanctions on Moscow.

items.text: Evernorth Holdings, which holds about 473 million XRP, was set to begin trading on Nasdaq as XRPN on Oct. 12 after completing its merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, the company said.
items.detail: Evernorth said it closed the business combination on Oct. 9 with about $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses, from investors including Arrington Capital, SBI Group, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR. It said it plans to deploy capital across the XRP economy and expected to ring the Nasdaq closing bell on Oct. 14.
items.why: Turns a closely watched crypto SPAC into a traded XRP-treasury stock on a federal holiday.

items.text: Russia kept striking Ukraine's power sites overnight, a day after President Trump announced an energy ceasefire, and Moscow still has not said it agreed.
items.detail: Kharkiv prosecutors said Russian forces hit an energy facility on the city's outskirts Monday, after Sunday-evening strikes on power plants in Kyiv and Kharkiv caused outages; energy and rail sites in the Zhytomyr region were also hit overnight. Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to stop striking Russian energy infrastructure if Russia does the same.
items.why: The truce Trump announced is not holding on the ground.

items.text: Two Indian sailors are missing after a drone hit the tanker Petro Dolphin off Oman's Sohar port, as Iran's Guards warned ships running dark will be treated as hostile.
items.detail: India's Foreign Ministry said Monday the two were among 11 Indian crew aboard the Petro Dolphin when it was struck Sunday near the Sohar anchorage, outside the Strait of Hormuz; a second tanker, the Valthera, was hit by a projectile and caught fire, but its crew is safe. Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said vessels that switch off navigation and identification systems in the strait will be dealt with as hostile, and claimed a third tanker struck a mine there Sunday.
items.why: Attacks on shipping are spreading beyond Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman.

upcoming.text: Supreme Court hears Beaird v. United States.
upcoming.detail: Whether courts must still defer to Sentencing Guidelines commentary under Stinson v. United States.
